intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: A multi-day guided trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes. Book a local guide from Pokhara's Lakeside district to save costs and support the local economy. Start early on Day 2 to maximize daylight trekking hours given the late Day 1 arrival. Stay in teahouses along the route to remain close to the trail and avoid long transfers.
experiences.location: Annapurna Sanctuary, Modi Khola Valley, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Viewpoint Hike
experiences.description: A shorter 2-day hike from Ghorepani to Poon Hill (3,210m) offering panoramic sunrise views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Machhapuchhre. Ideal for the first active days of the trip since it is accessible directly from Nayapul, close to Pokhara. Staying overnight in Ghorepani teahouses puts you right at the trailhead, eliminating wasted travel time.
experiences.location: Ghorepani and Poon Hill, Myagdi District, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk in Ghandruk
experiences.description: Explore the stone-paved lanes of Ghandruk, one of the largest Gurung villages in Nepal. Visit the Gurung Museum, interact with locals, observe traditional weaving, and enjoy authentic dal bhat at a family-run lodge. Ghandruk sits directly on the ABC and Poon Hill trekking routes, making it a natural overnight stop that adds cultural depth without detours.
experiences.location: Ghandruk Village, Kaski District, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: A less-crowded 4–5 day trek to Mardi Himal Base Camp (4,500m) with stunning close-up views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif. The trail starts from Forest Camp near Kande, just 45 minutes from Pokhara Lakeside, making it highly accessible. Teahouse accommodation along the route keeps you embedded in the trekking zone throughout.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal Trail, Lwang Ghalel, Kaski District, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Begnas Lake Kayaking and Nature Walk
experiences.description: A relaxing half-day activity at Begnas Lake, the second largest lake in the Pokhara Valley, surrounded by forested hills and Himalayan views. Rent a kayak or rowboat, then walk the quiet lakeside trails spotting migratory birds and local wildlife. This is an ideal activity for Day 2 morning before trekking begins, as it is only 15km from Pokhara Lakeside and allows a gentle acclimatization day after the late Day 1 arrival.
experiences.location: Begnas Lake, Rupa Rural Municipality, Kaski District, Pokhara Valley

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Complete immigration and baggage claim. Exchange currency at the airport (avoid hotel exchange rates). Take a local bus or shared taxi to Pokhara or arrange a budget transfer. If arriving in Pokhara by late afternoon, check into Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay and rest. Explore the immediate surroundings of your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into accommodation, freshen up. Take a short walk around the local area to get oriented. Visit a nearby local tea house or small restaurant for a welcome meal. Plan and review your 14-day trekking itinerary with the hotel staff.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or skip
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a local roadside eatery near the bus park (~300-400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal (Dal Bhat, vegetables, pickle) at a local teahouse (~400-500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel day. Carry USD cash for easier exchange. Confirm your trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) can be arranged the next morning in Pokhara. Keep hydrated during travel. Budget tip: local buses from Kathmandu to Pokhara cost ~800-1000 NPR vs ~5000+ NPR for tourist buses.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Pokhara trekking permit office. Obtain your Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP ~3000 NPR) and TIMS card (~2000 NPR) — essential for trekking. Pack your trekking bag with essentials: layers, rain gear, first aid kit, snacks, and a water purification system. Rent any missing trekking gear from local shops in Lakeside, Pokhara at budget rates.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (starting point of the Annapurna Circuit/Poon Hill trek). The journey takes about 1.5-2 hours and costs ~200-300 NPR. Begin the first stretch of trekking from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 2-3 hours walk, ~1,540m elevation). The trail passes through terraced fields, small villages, and lush subtropical forests.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tikhedhunga and check into a basic teahouse guesthouse (~500-800 NPR per night). Rest tired legs, enjoy the mountain village atmosphere. Interact with fellow trekkers and share route tips.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or egg toast at the hotel (~200-300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a local teahouse along the trail (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Vegetable noodle soup and milk tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~350-450 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Carry at least 2 liters of water. Purification tablets or a filter bottle save money on bottled water throughout the trek. Teahouse accommodation often comes with a free or discounted meal if you dine at their restaurant. Start trekking early to avoid afternoon haze. October is peak season — trails will be busy but weather is generally excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00-6:30 AM) to start the iconic climb from Tikhedhunga to Ulleri — a steep stone staircase of approximately 3,000 steps rising through rhododendron and oak forests. This challenging ascent takes 1.5-2 hours but rewards with stunning valley views. Reach Ulleri (~1,960m) and rest at a teahouse for a snack break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Ulleri through Banthanti to Ghorepani (~2,860m). The trail passes through dense rhododendron forests with occasional glimpses of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli peaks. The total walk from Ulleri to Ghorepani takes approximately 3-4 hours. Arrive at Ghorepani by early afternoon, check into a teahouse, and explore the village.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges from Ghorepani village. The golden hour light on the peaks is spectacular. Prepare gear and set an early alarm for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow (wake up at 4:30 AM). Join other trekkers at a communal teahouse dining area for warmth and conversation.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes with honey and black tea at Tikhedhunga (~250-350 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice and lemon tea at Ulleri teahouse (~400-450 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra rice (unlimited refills) at Ghorepani teahouse (~500-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The Tikhedhunga to Ulleri stairs are the hardest part of the Poon Hill trek — take it slow and steady. Ghorepani gets cold at night (can drop to 5-8°C in October) so use your sleeping bag liner. Teahouse rooms are basic but functional. Confirm wake-up time with teahouse staff for the Poon Hill sunrise hike.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 4:30 AM for the iconic Poon Hill sunrise hike. The 45-minute climb (3,210m) in the dark by headlamp leads to one of Nepal's most celebrated panoramas. Watch the sunrise illuminate Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and dozens more peaks in a 360-degree Himalayan panorama. Return to Ghorepani for a hearty breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: After breakfast, trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (~2,630m) via Deurali. This beautiful ridge walk through rhododendron and bamboo forests takes approximately 4-5 hours. The trail offers continuous mountain views. Arrive at Tadapani and check into a teahouse. Explore the small village and enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere compared to Ghorepani.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Tadapani teahouse with views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). Write journal notes or review photos from the spectacular Poon Hill sunrise. The evening sky at this elevation is stunning for stargazing if clouds permit.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and ginger tea after returning from Poon Hill (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Tibetan bread with jam and black tea at Deurali (~300-350 NPR)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry with rice and soup at Tadapani teahouse (~450-550 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is ~100 NPR. Arrive early to secure a good viewing spot as it gets crowded in October peak season. Bring warm layers — it's very cold before sunrise at 3,210m. The Ghorepani to Tadapani trail is less trafficked and more serene. Tadapani has fewer teahouses so accommodation is more peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (~2,170m), one of the most important villages on the Annapurna Sanctuary route. The trail descends steeply through forests before climbing back up to Chomrong. The walk takes approximately 3-4 hours with excellent views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre throughout. Chomrong is a large, well-developed village with good facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chomrong village — a beautiful Gurung settlement with stone-paved streets, terraced fields, and stunning mountain backdrops. Visit the local monastery and take in the incredible views of Annapurna South directly ahead. Rest and acclimatize. This is the last major village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary — stock up on any supplies needed.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a cultural evening if organized by your teahouse (some offer Gurung cultural performances). Chat with local Gurung families about their way of life. Plan the upcoming days into the Annapurna Base Camp sanctuary with your teahouse host who will provide updated trail conditions.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk and tea at Tadapani (~250-300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a trail-side teahouse between Tadapani and Chomrong (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (great for altitude), Dal Bhat at Chomrong teahouse (~500-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a local remedy for altitude sickness — highly recommended at higher elevations. Chomrong is the checkpoint for the Annapurna Sanctuary — your ACAP permit will be checked here. Stock up on snacks, energy bars, and water purification tablets as prices increase significantly above Chomrong. ATMs are not available beyond Pokhara so ensure you have enough cash (~15,000-20,000 NPR for the remaining trek).

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Chomrong, descend the famous Chomrong stone staircase to the Chomrong Khola river crossing, then begin the ascent through Sinuwa (~2,360m). The trail enters increasingly dense bamboo and rhododendron forest. Trek continues to Bamboo (~2,310m) — a small cluster of teahouses in a beautiful bamboo grove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo through Doban to Himalaya Hotel (~2,920m). The trail follows the Modi Khola river through a narrow gorge with towering walls. The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic as you enter the Annapurna Sanctuary. Watch for wildlife including Himalayan tahr, langur monkeys, and various bird species. Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Himalaya Hotel teahouse. The surrounding cliffs and forest create an atmospheric, enclosed feeling. Practice deep breathing exercises for acclimatization. The sound of the river rushing below is a natural soundtrack for the evening. Lights out early for another big day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Egg fried rice and black tea at Chomrong (~350-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup and biscuits at Bamboo teahouse (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra vegetables at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~550-650 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Note that prices increase significantly inside the Annapurna Sanctuary due to the remoteness — Dal Bhat may cost 600-800 NPR. This is normal and expected. The trail between Bamboo and Himalaya Hotel can be slippery — trekking poles are very helpful here. Watch for falling rocks in the gorge section. Leeches may be present in the forest sections despite October being drier — tuck trousers into socks.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel through Hinku Cave to Deurali (~3,230m). The trail continues through forest and begins emerging into more open terrain. Hinku Cave is a large rock overhang where trekkers historically sheltered — worth a brief stop. The landscape becomes more alpine and dramatic. Deurali marks the entrance to the upper sanctuary zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push from Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, ~3,700m). This section crosses the Modi Khola on a bridge and climbs steeply through the valley. The views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) become overwhelming as you approach MBC. Arrive at MBC and check into a teahouse. The mountain scenery here is absolutely jaw-dropping with peaks surrounding you on all sides.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset alpenglow on Machhapuchhre, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna from MBC. The colors shifting from gold to pink to purple on the massive ice faces are unforgettable. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol for acclimatization. Go to bed early for the ABC sunrise push tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and ginger tea at Himalaya Hotel (~350-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and crackers at Deurali teahouse (~500-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat and garlic soup at MBC teahouse (~700-800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: At 3,700m, altitude effects become noticeable — headaches, shortness of breath, and fatigue are common. Drink 3-4 liters of water daily. Move slowly and steadily. If you feel severe symptoms (persistent headache, nausea, confusion), descend immediately — never ascend with AMS symptoms. The teahouses at MBC are basic but adequate. Sleeping bags are essential at this elevation as temperatures drop well below freezing at night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake at 5:00 AM and trek the final 1-1.5 hours from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, ~4,130m) for sunrise. This is the emotional and physical pinnacle of the trek. Arrive at ABC as the first light hits the ring of eight peaks surrounding the sanctuary — Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Khangsar Kang, Tharpu Chuli, Hiunchuli, and the sacred Machhapuchhre. Stand in the heart of the Annapurna Sanctuary and absorb the 360-degree Himalayan amphitheater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning exploring around ABC. Visit the various viewpoints around the base camp area. Take photographs, meditate, or simply sit in awe of the surrounding giants. By midday, begin the descent back to MBC and continue down to Deurali or Bamboo to sleep at a lower, safer altitude. Descending 500-1000m for sleeping is recommended for acclimatization health.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo or Himalaya Hotel teahouse. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers over dinner. The descent will have been hard on the knees but spirits will be high. Rest well — the body recovers faster at lower altitude.

meals.breakfast: Hot chocolate and biscuits at ABC (~500-600 NPR)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at MBC on descent (~600-700 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra helpings at Bamboo/Himalaya Hotel (~550-650 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: ABC is the highlight of the entire trip — take time to fully experience it rather than rushing. Do not attempt to sleep at ABC unless you are well acclimatized — descend to a lower teahouse for sleeping. Carry a light daypack to ABC from MBC if possible. Weather at ABC can change rapidly — be prepared for wind and cold even in October. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience — be present and take it all in.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the return descent from your overnight teahouse (Bamboo/Himalaya Hotel area) back through the Annapurna Sanctuary. The descent through the bamboo forest and Modi Khola gorge is faster than the ascent. Trek back through Sinuwa toward Chomrong. The familiar trail feels different going downhill and in the opposite direction — notice new details and perspectives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Chomrong by midday. Rather than retracing your exact steps to Ghorepani, take the alternative route toward Jhinu Danda (~1,760m) — a small village famous for its natural hot springs on the Modi Khola river. The descent to Jhinu Danda takes approximately 1.5-2 hours from Chomrong.
day_by_day.evening: Soak tired trekking muscles in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs (entry ~200-300 NPR) — a perfect reward after days of high-altitude trekking. The hot springs sit beside the rushing Modi Khola river surrounded by jungle — a magical, restorative experience. Check into a basic teahouse at Jhinu Danda for the night.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at overnight teahouse (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at Chomrong teahouse (~500-600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and masala tea at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~450-550 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs at Jhinu Danda are one of the best-kept secrets of the Annapurna trek — don't miss them. They are most enjoyable in the late afternoon/evening. Bring flip-flops and a towel. The descent from Chomrong to Jhinu Danda involves a steep downhill section — trekking poles help protect knees. Jhinu Danda is a quiet, peaceful village with a beautiful riverside setting.

day_by_day.morning: Morning soak in the hot springs if you didn't get enough yesterday. Trek from Jhinu Danda to New Bridge (~1,340m) and continue to Landruk (~1,565m) — a beautiful traditional Gurung village with terraced fields and excellent views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South. The trail passes through subtropical forest and farming communities. This section is less trafficked and more authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Landruk village — walk through the traditional stone-paved paths, observe local Gurung farming life, and interact with villagers. The views from Landruk of Machhapuchhre are among the best anywhere. Continue trekking or rest in Landruk depending on energy levels. Alternatively, continue to Tolka (~1,700m) for a slightly higher overnight stop.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Machhapuchhre from Landruk or Tolka are spectacular. Enjoy a quiet evening in a traditional teahouse far from the main tourist crowds. The authentic village atmosphere here is a wonderful contrast to the busier sections of the trek.

meals.breakfast: Egg toast and black tea at Jhinu Danda (~250-300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable soup and Tibetan bread at New Bridge teahouse (~350-450 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with local vegetable pickle at Landruk/Tolka teahouse (~450-500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Landruk is an excellent example of a traditional Gurung village — take time to appreciate the architecture, terraced agriculture, and local culture. This section of the trek is often overlooked by trekkers rushing back to Pokhara — taking this alternative route rewards you with more authentic experiences and fewer crowds. Stock up on water here as the next section varies in water availability.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Landruk/Tolka through Potana (~1,890m) toward Dhampus (~1,650m). The trail passes through rhododendron forests with continuous mountain views. Dhampus is a popular village known for its panoramic views of the entire Annapurna range and is often used as a short trekking destination from Pokhara. The morning light on the peaks from Dhampus is magnificent.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Dhampus, descend to Phedi (~1,130m) where you can catch local transportation back to Pokhara. The drive takes approximately 30-45 minutes and costs ~200-300 NPR by local bus or shared jeep. Arrive in Pokhara by early afternoon. Check back into your Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay accommodation. Take a long hot shower — you've earned it.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna Base Camp trek with a lakeside stroll along Phewa Lake in Pokhara. Enjoy the reflection of the Annapurna range on the lake surface. Visit the Lakeside area (Baidam) for some post-trek relaxation. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate — still budget-friendly but a step up from teahouse fare.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and honey at Landruk/Tolka teahouse (~300-350 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at Dhampus teahouse (~400-500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal with local millet beer (Tongba) at a Lakeside Pokhara restaurant (~600-800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Congratulations on completing the Annapurna Base Camp trek! Total trekking distance covered over 10 days is approximately 110-120 km with 5,000m+ of elevation gain. Take time to appreciate this achievement. In Pokhara, check your body for any blisters, muscle issues, or signs of altitude-related illness that may need attention. Pokhara has good medical facilities. Laundry services in Lakeside are cheap (~500 NPR per load).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry ~400 NPR) — an excellent museum dedicated to the history of Himalayan mountaineering, local mountain cultures, and the geology of the Himalayas. Very relevant and enriching after your trekking experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake (~300-500 NPR per hour) and row to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake — a beautiful Hindu temple dedicated to the goddess Barahi. Explore the western shore of Phewa Lake where local fishing communities live. The reflections of Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range on the lake are iconic. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the hill above the lake for panoramic views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Himalayas.
day_by_day.evening: Browse the Lakeside market for budget souvenirs: Nepali handmade paper products, Thangka paintings, prayer flags, singing bowls, and trekking gear. Prices are negotiable — bargain respectfully. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a lakeside cafe watching the sunset over Phewa Lake.

meals.breakfast: Full English breakfast at a Lakeside cafe (~400-500 NPR)
meals.lunch: Momos (steamed dumplings) with chili sauce at a local Pokhara restaurant (~250-350 NPR)
meals.dinner: Newari set meal at a local restaurant away from the tourist strip (~500-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Day 12 is a well-deserved rest day. Let your body recover from the trek. If you have any gear rentals, return them today to avoid extra charges. The World Peace Pagoda can be reached by a 30-minute hike from the lakeside or by a short boat ride plus walk — the hike option is free and enjoyable. Stay hydrated and eat well to replenish your body after the demanding trek.

day_by_day.morning: Optional sunrise hike or paragliding from Sarangkot Hill (~1,592m) — the most popular viewpoint above Pokhara with stunning sunrise views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Local buses run to Sarangkot for ~100 NPR or it's a 1.5-hour hike from Lakeside. Budget paragliding from Sarangkot costs ~4,000-6,000 NPR (30 minutes) — a spectacular way to see the Himalayas from the air if budget allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) — two natural attractions near Pokhara (combined entry ~200 NPR). The cave contains a sacred Shiva shrine and connects underground to the Davis Falls waterfall. Explore the Seti River Gorge viewpoints where the river disappears underground through narrow gorges — a geological wonder. These are all within a short distance of each other and reachable by local tempo (~50 NPR).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Pokhara. Enjoy a sunset dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Lakeside with views of the Annapurna range for a memorable final night. Pack your bags for the return journey. Reflect on the incredible experiences of the past two weeks in the Himalayas.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and fresh fruit at Sarangkot viewpoint cafe (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable biryani at a local Pokhara restaurant (~350-450 NPR)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner: Dal Bhat with all accompaniments at a rooftop Lakeside restaurant (~700-900 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding from Sarangkot is genuinely budget-friendly by international standards and is a bucket-list experience — consider splurging if budget allows. Book paragliding operators directly at the launch site rather than through hotel touts to get better prices. Davis Falls is most impressive during/after monsoon season but still worth visiting in October. Begin packing tonight as Day 14 is your departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Pokhara. Complete any remaining souvenir shopping in the Lakeside market. Visit a local pharmacy if you need any trekking-related medical supplies to take home. Take a final walk along Phewa Lake and say goodbye to the Annapurna range — your trekking companion for the past two weeks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transportation from Pokhara to Kathmandu. Options: tourist bus (~800-1000 NPR, 6-7 hours), local bus (~500-600 NPR, 7-8 hours), or domestic flight (~5,000-8,000 NPR, 25 minutes — worth considering if time is tight). Arrive in Kathmandu and check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel if your international flight is the next day, or head directly to the airport if departing tonight. Allow extra time for Kathmandu traffic.
day_by_day.evening: If time permits before departure, take a quick evening walk through Thamel, Kathmandu's tourist hub. Visit the nearby Boudhanath Stupa (UNESCO World Heritage Site, entry ~400 NPR) — one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world and a deeply spiritual site. Do final souvenir shopping in Thamel. Head to the airport with plenty of time (arrive 3 hours before international departure).

meals.breakfast: Last Dal Bhat or Nepali breakfast at a Lakeside teahouse (~300-400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Snacks and local biscuits during travel (~150-200 NPR)
meals.dinner: Quick dinner at a Thamel restaurant or airport restaurant — try a final plate of momos (~400-600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Final budget summary: Accommodation (teahouses + hotel) ~14,000-18,000 NPR; Food ~25,000-30,000 NPR; Transport ~5,000-8,000 NPR; Permits ~5,000 NPR; Activities ~2,000-3,000 NPR; Miscellaneous ~3,000-5,000 NPR. Total estimated trip cost: ~55,000-70,000 NPR (~$400-520 USD) excluding international flights. Keep all your permit receipts as souvenirs. Nepal will stay with you long after you leave — the mountains, the people, and the peace of the Annapurna Sanctuary are truly life-changing.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Take a pre-arranged taxi or tourist bus to Pokhara (approx. 6–7 hours drive) or a domestic connecting flight to Pokhara (~25 min). Check into the Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation walk around the immediate surroundings to acclimatize to the altitude and environment.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade in Pokhara (if arriving via Pokhara as the gateway). Enjoy the mountain views at dusk. Visit the local bazaar area near the hotel for a relaxed introduction to Nepali culture.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or at Kathmandu airport café
meals.lunch: Quick dal bhat or momos at a roadside dhaba en route to Pokhara (~NPR 300–500)
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby mid-range Nepali restaurant — try Thakali set meal with rice, lentils, vegetables, and pickle (~NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel day. Keep evening activities light to rest for the trek ahead. Exchange currency at the airport or in Pokhara. Purchase a TIMS card and ACAP permit the next morning if not pre-arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) in Pokhara for panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges at sunrise. Hike up (~45 min) or take a boat across Phewa Lake and then walk up. Perfect acclimatization warm-up walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Project) office to obtain your ACAP permit and TIMS card if not already arranged. Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara to understand the Annapurna region's geography, culture, and mountaineering history. Pack and prepare your trekking gear for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lakeside (Baidam) area — browse trekking gear shops for any last-minute supplies. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Pokhara's tourist hub.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and Nepali tea (~NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Lakeside café lunch — try a sandwich or pasta with fresh juice (~NPR 500–700)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Lakeside — try Newari cuisine or a mixed grill platter with local Tongba millet beer (~NPR 700–1000)

day_by_day.notes: Permits required: TIMS card (~USD 20) and ACAP permit (~USD 30). Carry passport-size photos and photocopies of your passport. Confirm your trekking route with your guide or hotel staff. October is peak trekking season — weather should be clear and cool.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara by local jeep or tourist bus to Nayapul (approx. 1.5 hours). Begin the classic Annapurna Circuit / Poon Hill trek starting from Nayapul. Trek through terraced fields and rhododendron forests to Tikhedhunga (approx. 3–4 hours trekking, elevation ~1,540m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m) — a challenging but rewarding ascent of approximately 3,000 stone steps through dense forest. Arrive at Ulleri and rest at a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a cozy teahouse in Ulleri. Enjoy views of the surrounding hills and valley below. Interact with fellow trekkers and local villagers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — porridge, eggs, and tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch in Tikhedhunga — dal bhat or noodle soup (~NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ulleri — dal bhat set meal (the classic trekker's fuel, unlimited refills) (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 12–14 km. Elevation gain: ~1,000m. Carry at least 2 liters of water. The stone staircase to Ulleri is steep — take it slow and steady. Trekking poles highly recommended. October weather: crisp, clear skies, temperatures 10–18°C during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek from Ulleri through beautiful rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m). The trail gradually ascends through Banthanti and Nangethanti with stunning forest scenery. Arrive at Ghorepani in approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a teahouse and rest briefly. Take a short acclimatization hike around Ghorepani village. Explore the local area and interact with Magar and Gurung villagers. Optional: visit a local school or monastery.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike the next morning. Enjoy warm drinks around the teahouse fire. Watch the sunset paint the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges in golden hues from Ghorepani.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Ulleri — porridge with honey, eggs, and milk tea (~NPR 350–500)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop at Banthanti — vegetable noodle soup or fried rice (~NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ghorepani — dal bhat or pasta with garlic soup (~NPR 550–750)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 10 km. Elevation gain: ~900m. Ghorepani can be cold at night (0–5°C) — ensure your sleeping bag is rated for low temperatures. Set an alarm for 4:30 AM for the Poon Hill sunrise hike. The teahouses here are well-equipped with charging facilities (small fee applies).

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:30–5:00 AM) — hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) for one of the most iconic sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch the sun rise over Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South (7,219m), Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and over 20 other peaks. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) through spectacular rhododendron forests — one of the most beautiful forest trails in Nepal. The route offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife. Arrive in approximately 4–5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse in Tadapani. Enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere compared to Ghorepani. Watch the alpenglow on the Annapurna peaks at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Ghorepani after returning from Poon Hill — French toast, eggs, and hot chocolate (~NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or teahouse stop en route — energy bars, biscuits, and hot lemon tea
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Tadapani — pumpkin soup, dal bhat, or pasta (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: NPR 100. Bring a headlamp and warm layers for the pre-dawn hike. The rhododendron forest between Ghorepani and Tadapani is spectacular — October brings clear skies but the blooms are in spring (March–April). Total trekking distance today: approximately 13 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chhomrong (2,170m) — a picturesque Gurung village with stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. The trail descends steeply through forests before crossing a river and ascending to Chhomrong. Approximately 4–5 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village — one of the last permanent settlements on the Annapurna Sanctuary route. Visit the local monastery and interact with Gurung community members. The village is beautifully terraced with stone-paved pathways.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magnificent views of Annapurna South directly from Chhomrong. Relax on the teahouse terrace with hot tea. The evening sky in October is typically crystal clear — excellent stargazing opportunities.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Tadapani — muesli with yogurt, boiled eggs, and tea (~NPR 400–550)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch en route — dal bhat or veg fried rice (~NPR 450–600)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Chhomrong — try local Gurung cuisine if available, or standard dal bhat (~NPR 550–750)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 10–12 km. The descent from Tadapani to the river crossing involves steep stone steps — take care. Chhomrong is a checkpoint — have your permits ready for inspection. Stock up on snacks and water purification tablets as prices increase higher up the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and acclimatization day in Chhomrong. Take a gentle morning hike to the viewpoint above the village for unobstructed panoramas of the Annapurna massif. Visit the ACAP office in Chhomrong for information about the Sanctuary route ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional short hike to Sinuwa (2,360m) for a preview of the trail ahead and to assess fitness levels. Alternatively, explore the terraced farmland around Chhomrong and learn about local agricultural practices from villagers.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening at the teahouse — many teahouses in Chhomrong offer cultural programs or informal conversations with Gurung hosts about local traditions, festivals, and mountain life.

meals.breakfast: Full teahouse breakfast — pancakes with honey, eggs any style, and Nepali milk tea (~NPR 450–650)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the teahouse — vegetable soup and bread (~NPR 350–500)
meals.dinner: Special dinner at one of Chhomrong's better teahouses — try apple pie for dessert (a teahouse classic!) (~NPR 600–850)

day_by_day.notes: This is a strategic rest day before the more demanding high-altitude section into the Annapurna Sanctuary. Use this time to check and dry gear, treat any blisters, and ensure you're well-hydrated. The weather window in October is typically excellent — enjoy the clear mountain views.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong through Sinuwa and Bamboo to Dovan (2,600m). The trail enters the Modi Khola valley and passes through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest. Keep an eye out for wildlife including Himalayan tahr and various bird species. Approximately 5–6 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Dovan and check into a teahouse. The trail becomes more dramatic as the valley narrows and the towering walls of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre close in. Short afternoon rest and exploration of the immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: The valley walls create an impressive enclosed atmosphere at Dovan. Enjoy the sound of the Modi Khola river rushing below. Early dinner and rest — tomorrow is a long day.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Chhomrong — porridge, eggs, and tea (~NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Bamboo — dal bhat or noodle soup (~NPR 500–700, prices increase with altitude)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at Dovan — dal bhat, garlic soup (great for altitude), and hot ginger lemon honey (~NPR 600–800)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 11–13 km. The trail between Sinuwa and Bamboo can be slippery after rain — use trekking poles. Altitude increases gradually — watch for any signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness). Drink plenty of water. Note: teahouse facilities become more basic beyond Chhomrong.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan through Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and Hinku Cave to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m. The trail passes through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery as the valley opens up. The iconic fishtail peak of Machhapuchhre dominates the skyline. Approximately 6–7 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC and rest to acclimatize. Walk around the base camp area — the views of Machhapuchhre (6,993m) are absolutely breathtaking from here. The surrounding glacial moraines and high peaks create an otherworldly landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset colors on the surrounding peaks from MBC. The temperature drops significantly (can reach -5°C at night). Gather in the teahouse dining room for warmth and camaraderie with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at Dovan — porridge and hot drinks (~NPR 500–700)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Himalaya Hotel — dal bhat or fried rice (~NPR 600–800)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at MBC — dal bhat, garlic soup, and hot chocolate (~NPR 700–900)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 12–14 km. Significant elevation gain today (~1,100m) — go slowly and take frequent breaks. Drink 3–4 liters of water. Garlic soup is a traditional altitude remedy — have it at every meal. Avoid alcohol at altitude. Sleeping at MBC (3,700m) is your highest night so far — monitor for AMS symptoms.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (5:00 AM) — trek from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m for sunrise. The 1.5–2 hour walk through the glacial valley in the dark with a headlamp is magical. Arrive at ABC to witness one of the world's most spectacular mountain amphitheaters at sunrise — surrounded by Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC exploring the base camp area. Walk around the moraine to different viewpoints. Take photos and absorb the incredible scale of the Annapurna Sanctuary. Begin descent back to MBC after lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to MBC or continue down to Dovan for the night. Descending helps with acclimatization and recovery. Celebrate reaching ABC with a special teahouse dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hot drinks and snacks at ABC teahouse before the morning exploration (~NPR 400–600)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at ABC — simple but memorable given the location (~NPR 700–1000)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner at MBC or Dovan — celebratory dal bhat and apple pie (~NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the trek! ABC at 4,130m — watch for AMS symptoms. Do not push through severe headaches or vomiting. The descent back to lower altitudes is important for recovery. October weather at ABC: clear mornings, possible afternoon clouds. Temperature at ABC can drop to -10°C at night. The teahouses at ABC are basic but functional.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent from the Annapurna Sanctuary. Trek from overnight stop (Dovan or MBC) back through Bamboo and Sinuwa to Chhomrong. The descent is faster but harder on the knees — take your time on the steep stone steps. Approximately 5–6 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong — enjoy the warmer temperatures and lush surroundings after the high-altitude environment. Rest and recover. Visit the local tea shop for fresh apple tea and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Chhomrong — enjoy a hot shower (available at most teahouses here for a small fee). Reflect on the incredible journey to ABC over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast at overnight stop — eggs, toast, and tea (~NPR 500–700)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch en route — noodle soup or fried rice (~NPR 500–700)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Chhomrong — treat yourself to a more varied menu: pizza, pasta, or Nepali thali (~NPR 600–900)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 13–15 km. Descending requires different muscle groups — stretch your quadriceps and knees carefully. Use trekking poles for knee support. You're now on the return journey — maintain energy with regular snacks and hydration.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back to Ghorepani via Tadapani. This is a longer day but the trail is now familiar. Trek through the beautiful rhododendron and oak forests. Approximately 6–7 hours of trekking with significant elevation changes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani and check back into a teahouse. Optional: take a different trail variation to explore new viewpoints. Rest and recover from the long day.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the high mountains — enjoy the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri views from Ghorepani one last time. Optional second sunrise hike to Poon Hill the next morning if energy permits.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Chhomrong — pancakes and hot drinks (~NPR 450–650)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop at Tadapani — dal bhat (~NPR 500–700)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ghorepani — mixed menu with garlic naan and dal (~NPR 600–850)

day_by_day.notes: Total trekking distance: approximately 14–16 km. This is one of the longer days on the return — start early (7:00 AM) to avoid arriving after dark. The trail between Chhomrong and Tadapani involves a significant climb — pace yourself. Celebrate the near-completion of your trek with fellow trekkers over dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Optional early morning hike back up to Poon Hill for a second sunrise (highly recommended if energy allows — the experience is never the same twice). Return to Ghorepani for breakfast. Then trek down from Ghorepani through Ulleri and Tikhedhunga to Nayapul (approximately 5–6 hours descent).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a jeep or taxi back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours). Check back into accommodation in Pokhara. Enjoy a long hot shower and rest. Visit a massage parlor in Lakeside for a well-deserved post-trek massage (~NPR 1,500–2,500 for 60 min).
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara to mark the completion of the Annapurna trek. Explore the lively Lakeside area with its restaurants, cafes, and bars.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast in Ghorepani — full breakfast spread to fuel the descent (~NPR 450–650)
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch at Tikhedhunga or Nayapul — final dal bhat on the trail (~NPR 400–600)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a mid-range Pokhara restaurant — try Moondance Restaurant or similar for international/Nepali fusion cuisine (~NPR 1,000–1,500)

day_by_day.notes: The descent from Ghorepani to Nayapul is hard on the knees — take frequent breaks and use trekking poles. You've completed approximately 100+ km of trekking over the past 11 days — celebrate this achievement! In Pokhara, the Lakeside area has excellent restaurants, gear shops, and services.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Annapurna region. Wake up early for a boat ride on Phewa Lake at sunrise with Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range reflecting in the still water — one of Nepal's most iconic images. Visit the Barahi Temple on the lake island (small boat fee applies).
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring Pokhara's highlights: visit the Gupteshwor Cave and Davis Falls, or browse the Tibetan refugee camp and handicraft market for souvenirs. Pack your bags and prepare for departure. Take a final walk along the Lakeside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Pokhara's best restaurants — try Caffe Concerto or a rooftop restaurant with Himalayan views for a memorable final meal. Arrange airport transfer for your onward journey (domestic flight to Kathmandu or direct road transfer).

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and Nepali filter coffee (~NPR 500–800)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Lakeside café — sandwiches, salads, or momos (~NPR 500–700)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a quality restaurant: Nepali set menu with cultural performance, or international cuisine (~NPR 1,200–2,000)

day_by_day.notes: If departing from Kathmandu, allow enough time for the domestic flight (book in advance — Pokhara to Kathmandu is ~25 min by air or 6–7 hours by road). Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu can be busy — arrive 3 hours before international departures. Take home memories of the Himalayas, local souvenirs (Thangka paintings, pashmina, lokta paper products), and perhaps a jar of local honey!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to boutique lodge in the Annapurna Conservation Area via scenic helicopter or luxury charter vehicle. En route, enjoy your first breathtaking views of the Himalayan foothills. Check in, freshen up, and receive a personalized welcome briefing from your dedicated trek guide covering the 14-day itinerary, safety protocols, and gear check.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle acclimatization stroll around the lodge grounds and nearby village paths to absorb the mountain atmosphere. Watch the alpenglow paint the Annapurna massif at sunset from the lodge's panoramic terrace.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments and Nepali tea ceremony upon arrival at the lodge
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the lodge's fine-dining restaurant featuring curated Nepali and continental cuisine — dal bhat tarkari with organic local vegetables, grilled mountain trout, and warm apple crumble with cardamom cream

day_by_day.notes: Hydrate well upon arrival. Altitude awareness begins here. Lodge staff will provide a personalized altitude acclimatization plan. Luggage transfer is handled by porters. Lay out trekking gear for inspection tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Guided nature walk through rhododendron and oak forests surrounding the lodge. Your naturalist guide introduces local flora, fauna, and birdlife — look for Himalayan monal pheasants and lammergeiers. Light stretching and yoga session on the lodge deck at sunrise to prepare the body for trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Introductory half-day trek on a scenic lower trail with panoramic views of Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). Visit a traditional Gurung village, interact with locals, and learn about indigenous culture and architecture. Return to lodge by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxation hour with complimentary Himalayan herbal foot soak and massage at the lodge spa. Sunset cocktails on the terrace with mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Lavish lodge breakfast — fresh fruit platter, Tibetan bread with honey and yak butter, eggs to order, freshly brewed Himalayan coffee and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by lodge chefs, enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint on the trail — whole-grain wraps, local cheese, seasonal fruits, and energy bars
meals.dinner: Chef's table dinner featuring Newari-inspired cuisine — choila (spiced grilled meat), yomari dumplings, sautéed local greens, and saffron kheer for dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization and orientation day. Keep the pace gentle. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water. Trekking poles are recommended. Weather in October is typically clear and cool — ideal trekking season.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast followed by departure on the classic Annapurna Circuit trail segment. Trek through terraced farmlands, millet and buckwheat fields, and dense forests. First major ascent of the trip with rewarding valley views. Guided by expert local trekking guide with full porter support.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to a higher elevation checkpoint village. Explore a centuries-old Buddhist monastery with your guide — receive a blessing from the resident lama. Photography session capturing prayer flags, mani walls, and dramatic mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the night's premium teahouse or lodge accommodation. Unwind with a warm stone-heated shower. Briefing on the next day's route over hot ginger-lemon tea.

meals.breakfast: Power breakfast at the lodge — muesli with yak milk yogurt, boiled eggs, whole-grain toast, fresh juice, and Nepali masala tea
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at a curated teahouse on route — vegetable thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup), momos with tomato chutney, and butter tea
meals.dinner: Multi-course dinner at the premium teahouse — lentil soup, mixed vegetable curry, steamed rice, sautéed spinach, and warm apple pie

day_by_day.notes: Porter-to-trekker ratio ensures no guest carries more than a daypack. All accommodations are pre-vetted for cleanliness and comfort. Emergency satellite communication device carried by guide at all times.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a spectacular sunrise mountain view from a nearby ridge — one of the most iconic photo opportunities of the trip. Guided meditation session at a hilltop stupa as the peaks turn gold. Return for a hearty breakfast before the day's trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full-day trek through subtropical and temperate forest zones, crossing traditional suspension bridges over glacial rivers. Pass through Magar and Gurung ethnic villages. Cultural interaction with village elders arranged by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the evening's lodge. Enjoy a private cultural performance — traditional Gurung dance and music arranged exclusively for your group. Stargazing session with a telescope provided by the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Continental and Nepali fusion breakfast — granola, seasonal berry compote, fried eggs, Tibetan butter tea, and fresh-pressed juice
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed beside a glacial river — smoked chicken sandwiches, roasted nuts, energy bars, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Authentic Gurung feast prepared by a local family cook — gundruk soup, dhido (buckwheat porridge), smoked pork with local herbs, and sel roti with honey

day_by_day.notes: Altitude gain is gradual today. Watch for signs of altitude sickness — headache, nausea, dizziness. Guide carries supplemental oxygen and a comprehensive first-aid kit. Acclimatization rest stops are built into the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and acclimatization morning at the lodge. Optional gentle yoga and breathing exercises led by a certified instructor. Explore the immediate village surroundings independently or with a guide. Visit a local weaving cooperative to see traditional Himalayan textiles being made.
day_by_day.afternoon: Short acclimatization hike to a higher altitude viewpoint and return to the same lodge (classic acclimatization principle: climb high, sleep low). The hike rewards with close-up views of glaciers and high alpine terrain. Photography and journaling time at the summit viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa treatment at the lodge — deep-tissue massage using Himalayan salt and essential oils to relieve trekking fatigue. Private dinner with curated Nepali wine and spirits pairing.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast spread — eggs Benedict with local cured meat, fresh fruit salad, artisan bread, Himalayan honey, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch — vegetable fried rice, mixed salad, and warm lemon ginger broth
meals.dinner: Premium pairing dinner — Himalayan herb-marinated lamb chops, roasted root vegetables, creamy dal makhani, and chocolate fondant with vanilla cream

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization day is critical for health and safety at higher altitudes. Do not skip this day's protocol. Pulse oximeters available at the lodge for all guests. Guides monitor oxygen saturation levels morning and evening.

day_by_day.morning: Resume trek toward higher elevations. The landscape transitions dramatically from forested valleys to high-altitude alpine meadows. Trek through ancient trading routes historically used by Tibetan salt traders. Spot Himalayan tahr, blue sheep, and eagles with binoculars provided by the guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach a high-altitude village with sweeping 360-degree views of the Annapurna range. Visit a traditional Tibetan-influenced gompa (monastery). Participate in a butter lamp offering ceremony. Explore the village market for handcrafted souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into premium high-altitude lodge accommodation. Briefing on the upcoming high-altitude section of the trek. Enjoy a warming campfire (where permitted) under an impossibly star-filled sky.

meals.breakfast: High-energy breakfast — oatmeal porridge with dried fruits and nuts, scrambled eggs, whole-grain toast, and black tea with yak milk
meals.lunch: Hot teahouse lunch — tsampa (roasted barley) soup, vegetable curry with rice, and sweet Tibetan butter tea
meals.dinner: Hearty high-altitude dinner — thick lentil dal, aloo tama (potato and bamboo shoot curry), steamed rice, pickled vegetables, and warm rice pudding

day_by_day.notes: Temperatures drop significantly at higher altitudes — ensure all cold-weather gear is accessible in your daypack. Lodge provides high-quality down blankets and hot water bottles. Stay well hydrated and avoid alcohol at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: The most dramatic day of the trek — approach to the high pass. Early start before dawn to maximize clear weather windows. Trek through a moonscape of glacial moraines and rocky terrain. The panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Gangapurna, and Tilicho Peak is utterly awe-inspiring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Summit the high pass (Thorong La Pass at 5,416m if on the full circuit, or designated high-altitude viewpoint based on final route). Celebrate with a private champagne toast arranged by your guide team at the summit. Carefully descend to the next valley, enjoying a completely different cultural and geographical landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the descent-side lodge. Hot shower, medical check-in with guide, and a well-deserved full-body recovery massage. Early dinner and rest — this is the most physically demanding day of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn power breakfast — high-calorie porridge, boiled eggs, energy bars, and thermos of hot ginger tea to carry on the trail
meals.lunch: Summit celebration snack — premium energy bars, dark chocolate, dried fruits, nuts, and hot thermos tea at the pass
meals.dinner: Restorative dinner — rich bone broth soup, slow-cooked chicken curry, steamed vegetables, basmati rice, and warm barley pudding with cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: This is the highest point of the itinerary. Guests must be medically cleared for this altitude. Guide carries emergency descent medication (Diamox, dexamethasone) and supplemental oxygen. If any guest shows severe AMS symptoms, immediate descent protocol is activated. Helicopter evacuation insurance is strongly recommended and should be confirmed before this day.

day_by_day.morning: Gentle recovery morning with light stretching and breathing exercises. Explore the cultural richness of the Mustang-influenced village on the descent side — whitewashed monasteries, ancient cave dwellings, and fluttering prayer flags create a mystical atmosphere. Visit a local school supported by the lodge's community program.
day_by_day.afternoon: Easy descent trek through an arid, wind-sculpted landscape reminiscent of the Tibetan plateau. The terrain is dramatically different from the lush valleys — ochre cliffs, juniper shrubs, and vast open skies. Arrive at the next premium lodge for an extended rest afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography walk with your guide to a cliff-top viewpoint. Private dinner followed by a traditional Thakali cultural storytelling session arranged by the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Recovery breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, Tibetan bread, scrambled eggs with local herbs, and herbal recovery tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse lunch — Thakali set meal (a renowned local cuisine) featuring multiple curries, lentils, rice, and pickles
meals.dinner: Thakali specialty dinner — mustard-seed mutton curry, buckwheat bread, fermented vegetable salad, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Altitude is decreasing today — most guests feel significantly better. Continue hydrating well. The Mustang-influenced cultural zone is one of the most unique areas of Nepal — engage with your guide for deep cultural insights.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Tilicho Lake (one of the highest lakes in the world) or an equivalent premium nature experience based on route and conditions. Early departure through dramatic high-altitude terrain. The turquoise glacial lake surrounded by towering peaks is a once-in-a-lifetime sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Picnic lunch at the lakeside with a gourmet spread prepared by lodge chefs and carried by porters. Meditation and mindfulness session at the water's edge guided by your naturalist. Slow, scenic return trek to the lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the lodge for a celebratory evening — you have now completed the most challenging section of the Annapurna experience. Champagne reception on the terrace, followed by a bonfire gathering.

meals.breakfast: Energy-packed breakfast — granola with yak milk, boiled eggs, whole-grain toast, banana, and thermos of hot tea for the trail
meals.lunch: Lakeside gourmet picnic — artisan sandwiches, roasted vegetables, local cheese, fresh fruit, dark chocolate, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner — five-course tasting menu featuring the best of Nepali and continental cuisine, paired with premium Himalayan spirits

day_by_day.notes: Tilicho Lake sits at approximately 4,919m — acclimatization from previous days makes this manageable. Weather can change rapidly; guide carries emergency rain gear and thermal layers for all guests. Return time is flexible based on group pace.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent arc of the journey through lush lower valleys. Trek through dense rhododendron forests (spectacular color in October), passing cascading waterfalls and terraced rice paddies. Birdwatching session with your naturalist guide — over 400 species inhabit the Annapurna Conservation Area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a mid-elevation village famous for its hot springs. Enjoy a private natural hot spring soak — a deeply therapeutic experience after days of high-altitude trekking. The lodge arranges exclusive access to a premium hot spring pool with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at a beautifully appointed lodge in the lower valley. Explore the village bazaar for local crafts. Sunset from the lodge garden with cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast — fresh fruit, yogurt, honey, and herbal tea to prepare for the descent day
meals.lunch: Village teahouse lunch — dal bhat, seasonal vegetable curry, papad, and fresh lassi
meals.dinner: Romantic candlelit dinner at the lodge — grilled river fish, sautéed local greens, creamy mushroom soup, artisan bread, and mango kulfi for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs are a highlight of the lower Annapurna circuit. Water temperature is naturally regulated — guide will advise on safe soaking duration. Altitude-related symptoms should be largely resolved by now. Enjoy the increasing warmth and lushness of lower elevations.

day_by_day.morning: Trek through one of the most scenic gorges in the Himalayas — dramatic cliffs, roaring rivers, and ancient stone bridges create an extraordinary natural corridor. Your guide shares geological and ecological insights about the Kali Gandaki gorge, the world's deepest gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Thakali market town — explore its vibrant bazaar, ancient caravanserai ruins, and beautifully preserved old quarter. Arranged visit to a local home for a private cooking demonstration of Thakali cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Premium lodge stay in the market town. Rooftop dinner with sweeping valley views. Live traditional music performance arranged for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast — eggs to order, fresh-baked bread, seasonal fruit, yogurt, and specialty Himalayan tea
meals.lunch: Market town restaurant lunch — freshly made momos, thukpa, and Tibetan butter tea in a heritage dining room
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner with valley views — slow-roasted lamb with Himalayan spices, sautéed seasonal vegetables, artisan bread, and warm chocolate brownie with cream

day_by_day.notes: The Kali Gandaki gorge section is one of the most photographed landscapes in Nepal. Bring extra memory cards. Wind can be strong in the gorge in the afternoon — light windproof layers recommended. The cooking demonstration is a genuine cultural exchange — tips for the host family are appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final full trekking day — a beautiful walk through lower subtropical forests and terraced farmland back toward the Annapurna foothills base area. Visit the sacred Muktinath Temple complex — one of the most important pilgrimage sites for both Hindus and Buddhists, with 108 water spouts and an eternal flame.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the final trekking lodge. Celebration lunch with the entire guide and porter team. Tip ceremony and heartfelt farewell to your support team. Afternoon at leisure — reflect, journal, and soak in the last mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the lodge's finest dining room. Personalized certificate of achievement presented to each trekker. Slideshow of professional photos taken throughout the journey by the guide team.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory breakfast — full spread of Nepali and continental favorites, fresh-squeezed juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Team celebration lunch — traditional Nepali feast with all guides and porters, featuring dal bhat, multiple curries, and local sweets
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — premium seven-course tasting menu with Himalayan trout, organic lamb, seasonal vegetables, artisan cheeses, and a signature Annapurna dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Tip envelopes for guides and porters should be prepared in advance — your trip coordinator will provide guidance on appropriate amounts. The farewell ceremony is a meaningful tradition — take time to express gratitude to your team. Professional photo album will be couriered to your home address post-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in the Annapurna Conservation Area. Optional sunrise hike to a nearby viewpoint for last panoramic mountain views. Photography session with your guide. Pack up and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle or scenic mountain flight transfer back toward Pokhara. En route, stop at the iconic Peace Pagoda (World Peace Stupa) above Phewa Lake for panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Check into a premium lakeside resort in Pokhara.
day_by_day.evening: Lakeside dinner at Pokhara's finest restaurant with views of Phewa Lake and the Annapurna silhouette. Celebrate the completion of the trek with a special dessert and sparkling wine. Stroll along the Lakeside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast — leisurely spread with all favorites, fresh juice, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch at the Peace Pagoda viewpoint or en route restaurant — wood-fired pizza, fresh salads, and lemonade
meals.dinner: Lakeside fine dining in Pokhara — grilled Himalayan trout with herb butter, truffle risotto, seasonal salad, and a signature chocolate tart with gold leaf

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is one of Nepal's most beautiful cities — the lakeside setting with Annapurna backdrop is magical. The premium resort offers full spa facilities, swimming pool, and concierge services. This is a well-deserved luxury transition day after the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal. Sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake with views of Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range reflected in the water — a serene and unforgettable farewell to the Himalayas. Return to resort for a luxurious final breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure time at the resort — optional spa treatment, swimming, or last-minute souvenir shopping at Pokhara's Lakeside market for premium Nepali handicrafts, thangka paintings, and pashmina. Private luxury transfer to Pokhara Airport for flight to Kathmandu, then onward international connection.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Nepal with extraordinary memories, a deep connection to the Himalayas, and a profound sense of accomplishment. Safe travels home.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort — full buffet spread with international and Nepali options, fresh juices, specialty coffee, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge — sandwiches, salads, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or Kathmandu airport premium lounge dinner depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits, receipts, and documents are collected for your records. The Annapurna Conservation Area entry permit and TIMS card should be retained as souvenirs. Your trip coordinator will provide a detailed post-trip report including GPS tracks, photos, and recommendations for future Himalayan adventures. Allow ample time for airport check-in — Kathmandu airport can be busy. Namaste and safe travels!
